situation: Your partner forgot your birthday, and you're hurt.
say: It's fine. Whatever. I'm used to it.
better: I felt hurt that you forgot my birthday. It matters to me. Can we talk about it?
also: Honestly, I was upset about my birthday, and I want you to know that.
weak: You never care about me, you only care about yourself.
Nothing happened. I'm fine.
why: Name the feeling with 'I', instead of sulking or attacking.

situation: You shouted during a fight and want to apologise.
say: Sorry if you felt bad.
better: I'm sorry I raised my voice. You didn't deserve that, and I'll work on it.
also: I was wrong to shout at you. I'm sorry.
weak: Okay, sorry. Happy now?
Sorry, but you also started it.
why: A real apology names what you did, with no 'if' and no 'but'.

situation: You feel jealous when your partner texts a friend late at night.
say: Why are you always talking to her? Who is she, actually?
better: I feel a bit insecure when you text Priya late at night. Can you help me understand?
also: This is my own insecurity, but I wanted to be honest that it's bothering me.
weak: Show me your phone, right now.
Fine, talk to her only. Why do you need me?
why: Own the jealousy as your feeling instead of accusing.

situation: You've hardly spent any time together for weeks.
say: You don't have time for me at all.
better: I miss us. Could we keep Sunday evenings just for the two of us?
also: I'd love more time with you. Can we plan one proper date a week?
weak: I know, your work is more important than me.
Do whatever you want, I don't care anymore.
why: Ask for what you want, not only for what's missing.

situation: You've had a draining day and need an evening alone.
say: Just leave me alone.
better: I need some time to myself tonight. It's not about you. I'll call you tomorrow.
also: I'm drained. Can I have a quiet evening, and we talk tomorrow?
weak: Don't call me. I'll call when I feel like it.
Nothing, I'm fine, why do you keep asking?
why: Ask for space with a reason and a time, so it doesn't feel like rejection.

situation: Your partner cancels your plans at the last minute, again.
say: As usual. I knew it.
better: I'm disappointed. It's the third time this month. Can we make plans you're sure you can keep?
also: I get that work came up, but I was looking forward to this. Let's fix a new time now.
weak: No problem, it's okay, I'll just sit at home.
You never keep your word. You're so unreliable.
why: Be honest about the pattern and ask for a change, without labels.

situation: You're deciding where to eat tonight.
say: Anything is fine, you decide.
better: I'm in the mood for South Indian. How about that new dosa place?
also: I'd like something light. Thai or South Indian?
weak: Anything, but not Chinese, not pizza, not that place, not...
You decide. You always decide anyway.
why: Say what you'd like. 'Anything' puts the whole decision on them.

situation: Your partner is upset after a bad day at work.
say: Don't be sad yaar, chill, it's not a big deal.
better: That sounds really hard. Do you want advice, or do you just want me to listen?
also: I'm here. Tell me what happened.
weak: You're overthinking. Just forget it.
At least it's not as bad as what happened to me.
why: Listen first and ask what they need. Don't brush feelings away.

situation: You want to talk about a future together, including marriage.
say: My parents are asking, so tell me, are you serious or not?
better: I've been thinking about our future. Can we talk about where we both see this going?
also: I'm serious about us. I'd like to know how you feel about the next step.
weak: Decide fast, my parents are already looking for matches.
Whatever happens, happens. Let's not think about it.
why: Share your own wish first, then invite theirs, without an ultimatum.

situation: Your partner made a joke about you in front of friends.
say: Okay, very funny. Ha ha.
better: That joke at dinner stung. I know you didn't mean harm, but please don't do that in front of friends.
also: Can we talk about that joke tonight? It embarrassed me.
weak: You insulted me in front of everyone. You always do this.
Nothing. I'm not talking to you.
why: Raise it in private, say how it felt, and make a clear request.

situation: You rarely tell your partner what you love about them.
say: You know na I love you, why should I say it?
better: I don't say it enough, but I love how you look after everyone around you.
also: Thank you for today. You made everything easier.
weak: Obviously I love you, don't be filmy.
Haan haan, love you too. Bye.
why: Specific appreciation lands far better than love that's just assumed.

situation: Decisions about your life as a couple keep being made by your partner's parents.
say: Your mother is always interfering in our life.
better: I feel left out when decisions about us are made at your parents' place. Can we decide together first?
also: I respect your parents. I'd just like us to agree on things before we share them.
weak: Choose: me or your family.
Fine, let your mother decide everything then.
why: Talk about the situation and your need, not an attack on their family.

situation: You're worried about how much the two of you are spending.
say: You are spending too much, we can't afford all this.
better: I'm worried about our savings. Can we sit down this weekend and plan a monthly budget together?
also: Let's agree how much each of us spends freely, and how much we save.
weak: You have no sense of money at all.
Fine, spend. We'll see what happens at month end.
why: Make money a shared plan, not a blame game.

situation: Your partner scrolls on their phone all through dinner.
say: Keep your phone aside, I'm not talking to a wall.
better: Can we keep our phones away during dinner? I really like our time to talk.
also: Phone-free dinners this week? I miss talking to you.
weak: Marry your phone then.
Okay, I'll also use my phone, no problem.
why: Make a simple request and say why it matters to you.

situation: After an argument, your partner has stopped talking to you.
say: Fine, don't talk. Who cares.
better: I don't like it when we stop talking. I'm ready to listen whenever you are.
also: I know you're upset. Can we talk once we've both calmed down?
weak: If you don't talk now, don't talk ever.
Okay, I'll also not talk. Let's see who breaks first.
why: Keep the door open instead of matching silence with silence.

situation: Your partner asks 'What's wrong?' and something is bothering you.
say: Nothing. I'm fine.
better: I'm upset about this morning. Give me ten minutes, then I'd like to talk about it.
also: Something's bothering me. Can we talk after dinner?
weak: You should know what's wrong.
Why would anything be wrong? Everything is just perfect.
why: Say that something is wrong. Making them guess leads to bigger fights.

situation: You've decided to end the relationship.
say: It's not you, it's me. Let's be friends.
better: I've thought about this a lot. I don't see a future for us, and I don't want to keep pretending.
also: This is hard to say, but I want to end things. You deserve honesty.
weak: I'm very busy these days, let's talk later. (And never call.)
You've changed. You're not the person I liked.
why: Be honest and kind. Vague lines leave the other person confused.

situation: In a long-distance relationship, your partner skipped yesterday's call.
say: You didn't call yesterday. Forget it.
better: I missed hearing from you yesterday. Can we fix a call time that works for both of us?
also: I know your shifts are long. Even a two-minute call helps me.
weak: You've found someone else, haven't you?
Okay, call only when you feel like it.
why: Turn the complaint into a simple plan you both agree on.

situation: You're doing most of the housework and you're tired of it.
say: I am doing everything in this house alone.
better: I'm tired of handling all the cooking. Could you take over dinners on weekdays?
also: Can we split the chores? I'll do mornings, you do evenings.
weak: You just sit and watch TV like a guest.
Leave it, I'll do it, as always.
why: A specific ask gets results. 'Everything' starts a fight.

situation: Your partner has sincerely apologised after a fight.
say: Hmm. Okay. Let's see.
better: Thank you for saying that. I accept it, and I'm glad we talked.
also: That means a lot. Let's move on.
weak: Sorry is not enough. You'll pay for this.
It's okay, it's okay, I'm used to it.
why: Accept a real apology clearly, so you can both move on.

situation: You want the mountains for your holiday; your partner wants the beach.
say: We always do what you want. This time Manali, final.
better: I'd really like the mountains this time. Could we do Manali now and Goa on the next trip?
also: Let's each list our top two places and find one we both like.
weak: Fine, Goa. I'll just sit in the hotel.
If it's not Manali, I'm not going.
why: State your preference and offer a fair trade.

situation: Your partner feels jealous of a colleague you often mention.
say: You are being so insecure, it's just a colleague!
better: I can see this is worrying you. Nikhil is just a colleague, and I'm happy for you to meet him.
also: I get why it felt odd. Ask me anything; I've nothing to hide.
weak: Your jealousy is your problem, not mine.
Okay, I'll stop talking to all my colleagues then.
why: Reassure and stay open instead of calling their feeling silly.

situation: Your partner said yes to a Saturday plan for both of you without asking.
say: Why didn't you ask me before? I'm not coming.
better: I wish you'd checked with me first. I can't make Saturday, but I'd love to go another weekend.
also: Next time, can we check plans together? Saturday doesn't work for me.
weak: You never consider me. You just decide everything.
Fine, I'll come, but don't expect me to enjoy it.
why: Say no clearly, ask for a change next time, and offer another option.

situation: You want to understand what makes your partner feel loved.
say: Tell me na, what do you want from me?
better: What's one small thing I do that makes you feel loved? I'd like to do more of it.
also: When do you feel most cared for by me?
weak: What more do you want? I'm already doing so much.
I don't understand you at all.
why: Curious questions build closeness. Defensive ones shut it down.

situation: Lately you feel your partner takes you for granted.
say: Nobody values me in this relationship.
better: Lately I feel taken for granted. A thank-you now and then would mean a lot to me.
also: I'd like to feel more appreciated. Small things matter to me.
weak: You'll realise my value when I'm gone.
Fine, from tomorrow I'll also stop doing anything.
why: Say the feeling, and the small thing that would help.
